paper_title: The Median is Easier than it Looks: Approximation with a Constant-Depth, Linear-Width ReLU Network
authors: Abhigyan Dutta, Itay Safran, Paul Valiant
statement: Consider the following game. Alice’s favorite positive integer is r. Alice finds d′ balls arbitrarily arranged at locations x on the real line; and then a random subset S of n of these balls is colored red. Alice now (arbitrarily) chooses a real interval I such the number of red balls in I is her favorite number, |S ∩ I| = r. What can we say about the overall number of balls in I, regardless of how Alice chooses I? Intuitively, since dn′ fraction of the balls are red, this number |x ∩ I| should be ′ roughly r dn , and we show this is true in Lemma 28.
